name: TX-14
label: Safe R

key_factors: District leans Republican by about 12 points, a steep structural hurdle for the challenger
Weber holds an overwhelming money advantage: roughly $900K on hand versus about $5K for Bartie, with no outside spending to close the gap
Prediction markets price Weber at about 98% to win
No public polls or expert ratings flag the race as remotely competitive
model.rationale: Everything measurable points one direction: a 12-point Republican lean, a two-term incumbent, a fundraising gap of more than 25-to-1, and markets at 98% Republican. With no polls suggesting otherwise, a modest shift toward Safe R from the fundamentals-only estimate is justified by the total absence of any competitive signal.
model.watch: The race would only merit reconsideration if late polling showed a single-digit contest or a sudden influx of outside spending against Weber materially narrowed the financial gap.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Texas's 14th District, covering the Gulf Coast including Beaumont-Port Arthur and Galveston, leans Republican by about twelve points. Randy Weber has held the seat since 2013 and enters the general election with roughly $900,000 on hand after raising more than $1 million. Democratic nominee Thurman Bartie has raised about $37,000 and reported just over $5,000 in cash, with no outside spending reported on either side.

No public polls target the race and no national ratings groups list it as competitive. Prediction markets give Weber about a 98 percent chance of winning. The combination of a strongly Republican electorate, incumbency, and an overwhelming financial gap makes an upset improbable; Bartie would need a dramatic, unforeseen shift in the district's fundamentals to put the seat in play.
